steps: Curl both index fingers into hooked X shapes, as if each hand is pinching a tiny slip of paper.
Hold both hooked hands in front of your chest, about a foot apart.
Circle the two hands around each other once, trading places in the air.
End with both hands back where they started, the X hooks facing each other.
Keep a neutral face — the circling shows a straight swap with no tricks.
tip: The hands trade places in the air but land where they began, like swapping two items and staying put.

steps: Press your thumbs together with the other fingers tucked into loose fists.
Hold the joined hands a few inches in front of your chest or upper belly.
Push both hands smoothly forward about six inches, away from your body.
Keep both palms angled downward for the whole forward glide.
Hold a steady, determined face — the motion says the action keeps going.
tip: Push forward hard and stop dead, and CONTINUE becomes PERMANENT.

steps: Close your dominant hand into an S fist, thumb resting across the fingers.
Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat in front of you, palm facing up.
Circle the S fist once just above the open palm.
Land the side of the S fist down onto the open palm.
Keep the circle small and smooth, like one turn of the year.
tip: An S circling down onto the palm pictures the cycle of the four seasons; many signers fingerspell SEASON for TV or sports seasons.

steps: Extend your dominant index finger, keeping the other fingers curled into your palm.
Hold your arm out in front of you with the palm facing up.
Draw a small circle, about the size of a quarter, with your index fingertip.
Drive the circle from your arm, keeping the wrist steady and relaxed.
Keep your face neutral — the sign names a plain, unspecified person.
tip: The same sign also means something, single, alone, or only — context picks the meaning.

steps: Point your non-dominant index finger straight up in front of your chest, like a small post.
Shape your dominant hand into a V, index and middle fingers extended and spread.
Bring the V hand down over the upright finger so the finger rests between the two prongs.
Aim the V fingertips downward as the hand settles onto the finger.
Keep a businesslike, neutral expression — this is the paperwork version of apply.
tip: A second popular version looks like VOLUNTEER and means apply for or run for office; the V-over-1 version covers apply to, application, and file.

steps: Open your dominant hand flat, fingers together and extended.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing down.
Slide the flat dominant hand across the back of the non-dominant hand, from one side to the other.
Keep the dominant palm facing down as it glides over the back of the other hand.
Make the pass in one clean stroke — the crossing path is the whole meaning.
tip: This is the same sign as OVER — it also covers across and after in time.

steps: Pinch your dominant thumb and index finger together into a small pincer, like holding a stamp.
Raise your non-dominant index finger upright in front of your chest, palm angled sideways.
Tap the pinching hand once against the side of the upright finger.
Angle the pinching hand's palm toward the finger as it taps.
Keep your face neutral — one tap names the machine that prints.
tip: Same sign as PRINT — context decides whether you mean the action or the machine; a person who prints is PRINT plus PERSON.

steps: Close your dominant hand into an A fist, thumb pressed along the side of the fingers.
Hold the fist in front of your chest with the palm facing left and the thumb-side up.
Twist your wrist so the hand finishes palm down, thumb-side still facing left.
Make the twist one smooth turn, like sweeping through every option.
Pair it with a casual, open face — anything goes.
tip: The ANY sign doubles as ANYTHING; adding the separate THING sign after it is optional, not required.
